chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazam who said:

I entered the bathhouse with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). So when he came out to the dressing room, he called for an incense burner and applied the incense with it. Then he said: 'Apply the incense, O Murazam.' I said, 'The one who wants to take his share, can he take it?' He said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sharing incense in the bathhouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) illustrates the practical etiquette of personal hygiene and social generosity within the Shia tradition. By instructing Muramim to allow others to partake in the incense, the Imam emphasizes that ritual purity items are not merely private possessions but opportunities for communal benefit and ease. This incident underscores the Islamic value of facilitating comfort for others, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual and social grace.
